real_task: Discover the authenticated GitHub connector operations and exact schemas needed to publish this session's tested commit without shell credentials.
observed_problem: Agent 2 showed that the two positive tool-discovery reports compared names-first against broad full-entry queries, not the simpler targeted full-entry alternative.
baseline: One targeted full-entry registry query for GitHub repository fetch, blob, tree, commit, branch, comparison and non-force ref update operations.
intervention: A names-only targeted pass followed by exact-schema retrieval for the operations selected for publication.
hypothesis: Names-first plus exact-schema retrieval uses at least 2000 fewer serialized registry bytes than a targeted full-entry query while retaining every operation required for successful publication.
quality_control: Both conditions must expose the complete required operation set; the selected exact schemas must support a successful branch/commit/ref publication and remote tree verification.
overhead: Count every discovery response in each condition, publication verification, this trace and report maintenance. Do not infer token, latency or LLM-quality gains from bytes.
stop_condition: Run one comparison on this registry snapshot and build no helper. If a comparable targeted full-entry query is unavailable, any required operation is missed, publication fails, or payloads cannot be measured from returned data, record inconclusive and stop the family.

result.quality: All seven required operations and exact schemas were present; publication quality remains a separate end-of-session check.
failed_measurement_calls: The first registry instrumentation expression failed before returning data because TextEncoder was unavailable; the retry used an explicit UTF-8 byte counter.
limitations: The targeted query still returned 41 irrelevant entries, so it does not falsify Agent 2's modeled careful-query break-even.
If exact operation names are already trustworthy, direct exact retrieval is 2145 bytes smaller than names-first on this snapshot.
The full registry is runtime-provided metadata here; results may not transfer to a deferred-tool harness.
Order effects, time, tokens, model quality, downstream success and documentation maintenance were not compared end to end.
result.reason: The narrow byte threshold passed against one verb-targeted query, but the strongest simple alternative was not beaten and full utility overhead was not comparable. Together with Session 016, this is the second inconclusive tool-discovery evaluation.
